how.title: How it works
how.intro: This JSON to HTML converter turns a pasted response or local file into semantic HTML. Choose Table for data you want to scan across rows, or List for a document with many levels. Conversion happens in a Web Worker in your browser. The JSON text is not sent to our server, and you do not need an account.
how.arrayObjectsResult: One table with a header row. Columns include every key seen across the objects, in first-seen order. Missing values leave empty cells.
how.objectResult: A two-column table with keys in row headers and their values beside them.
how.nestedResult: A nested table for objects or arrays of objects. An array of simple values becomes a list inside its cell.
how.simple: A simple value or array of simple values
how.simpleResult: A single-cell table, or a one-column table for an array. Null and empty values leave empty cells.
how.layouts: Use Table for records such as orders, contacts and API responses. Use List when the hierarchy matters more than columns: objects become definition lists, and arrays become unordered lists. You can switch layouts after converting without pasting again. In either layout, the result uses text content only. Characters that could form HTML markup are escaped, so a value such as an image tag appears as text.
how.outputs: Table only gives you an HTML fragment to paste into a CMS, email template or existing page. Full HTML page adds a document wrapper, a title, a viewport setting and a small table style. Download that version if you want to open the result as a standalone file. Preview shows the HTML in a sandboxed frame; HTML code shows what will be copied or downloaded.
how.limits: You can paste text or choose a .json or .txt file up to 50 MB. The preview shows at most 500 top-level rows to keep the page responsive; copying and downloading use the complete result. For very large output, the code panel shows only the start, but Copy HTML and Download HTML file still use everything. Numbers keep their JSON spelling. When a browser cannot preserve a large integer through JSON.parse, the converter keeps its original digits and shows a warning.
how.errors: If the JSON cannot be parsed, the message points to a line and column and suggests a fix. Common causes are trailing commas, single quotes, unquoted keys and comments. JSON Lines files contain one value per line rather than a single JSON array; use Wrap lines into an array to convert them, then run the conversion again.

excel.howNumbersResult: As shown in Excel keeps each cell’s format, such as $1,234.50, 12.5% or a ZIP code with its leading zero. Plain numbers gives 1234.5 and 0.125. Cells with the General format keep up to 15 significant digits either way, as Excel stores them.

excel.howMergedResult: The value goes in the first cell of the merged area. The other cells are empty.

excel.howFormattingResult: Left out. A CSV holds only values.
excel.howSeparators: Comma is the standard CSV separator and works in most apps and databases. Pick Semicolon for Excel in countries that use a comma as the decimal mark, such as Germany, France, Spain and Brazil, or when an importer asks for it. Tab gives you a .tsv file, which helps when your values contain many commas. A value that contains the separator, a double quote or a line break is wrapped in double quotes, as RFC 4180 describes, and each row ends with CRLF.
excel.howEncoding: The file is UTF-8, so accented letters, other scripts and emoji come through. Pick UTF-8 with BOM if you will open the CSV in Excel: without the byte order mark, Excel for Windows can show characters such as é as Ã©. Leave it off for databases, code and most import forms, where the BOM can end up in the first column name.
excel.howLimits: You can convert .xlsx, .xlsm, .xlsb, .xls and .ods files up to 50 MB. Large workbooks take longer on a phone and can run out of memory there; a computer handles more. The preview shows the first 100 rows and 30 columns, and the download has everything. Empty rows and columns at the end of a sheet are trimmed, and every row has the same number of fields.
excel.howErrors: A password-protected workbook can’t be read, so remove the password in Excel first. If a file can’t be read, it may be damaged, or it may be another format saved with an Excel extension: open it in Excel and save it as .xlsx. Some apps save formulas without their results, and those cells come out empty; open and save the file in Excel to calculate them.

jsonExcel.howArrayResult: One row per object, under a header row. Columns include every key seen across the objects, in first-seen order. Missing values leave empty cells.
jsonExcel.howObjectResult: Columns named with dots, such as shipping.city and shipping.address.zip.
jsonExcel.howList: A list of objects inside a record
jsonExcel.howListResult: With Separate sheets, a sheet named after the key, such as items. Its first column gives the row it belongs to, matching the # column on the parent sheet. With Numbered columns, columns such as items.1.sku and items.2.sku on the same sheet.
jsonExcel.howSimpleListResult: One cell, with the values separated by commas: red, blue. A list that holds other lists keeps its JSON text.
jsonExcel.howRoot: One object at the top level
jsonExcel.howRootResult: One row. Lists of objects inside it go on their own sheets, so a response such as {"users": […]} gives you a users sheet.
jsonExcel.howGridResult: Each inner array becomes a row as it is, with no header row added.
jsonExcel.howValues: Numbers and true or false keep their types, so you can sum, sort and filter them. Text stays text, even when it looks like a number, so ZIP codes and phone numbers keep their leading zeros. Dates written as 2024-01-15, 2024-01-15 14:30 or 2024-01-15T14:30:00Z become Excel dates; a Z time stays in UTC. A time with an offset, such as +02:00, stays as text so its clock time doesn’t change. Whole numbers with more than 15 digits, such as order IDs, are saved as text, because Excel keeps only 15 significant digits. Null leaves an empty cell.
jsonExcel.howNested: Choose Separate sheets when records contain lists, such as orders with line items. Each record stays on one row, and the list items go on their own sheet, which you can match back with the # columns using XLOOKUP or a pivot table. Choose Numbered columns when the lists are short and you want everything on one sheet. Every sheet has a filter on its header row and column widths that fit its first rows.
jsonExcel.howLimits: You can paste text or choose a .json, .jsonl or .txt file up to 50 MB. JSON Lines files, with one record per line, become one row per line. Excel allows 1,048,576 rows and 16,384 columns per sheet and 32,767 characters per cell. You’ll see a message if a sheet would be too large, and longer text is cut to fit, with a note. Large files take longer on a phone and can run out of memory there; a computer handles more. The preview shows the first 100 rows and 30 columns of each sheet, and the download has everything.
jsonExcel.howErrors: If the JSON can’t be parsed, the message points to a line and column and suggests a fix. Common causes are trailing commas, single quotes, unquoted keys and comments.

privacy.description: How thetoolproject handles files, contact emails, and basic website request data.
privacy.heading: Privacy policy
privacy.lead: Your files stay on your device when you use our conversion tools.
privacy.pFiles: The conversion tools process files and pasted text in your browser. We do not receive or store the files you choose, the text you paste, or the results you download. You do not need an account to use the tools.
privacy.pWeb: When your browser loads the site, the hosting provider receives information needed to serve it, which may include your IP address, browser details, and the pages requested. Hosting providers may keep routine request and security logs under their own policies.
privacy.pAnalytics: We use Google Analytics to learn which pages people visit and which tools and buttons they use, such as how often a conversion is started and whether it succeeds. Google Analytics sets cookies and receives your IP address, browser and device details, and the pages you view, and Google handles this data under <a:google>{googleLink}</a:google>. We send it only coarse details about your files, such as the file type and a size range. It never receives your file names, file contents, the text you paste, or your results. You can block analytics with your browser's cookie or content-blocking settings.
privacy.pMessages: If you email <a:email>{emailLink}</a:email>, we receive your email address and whatever you include in your message. We use that information to read and respond to you and to address the issue you raised. Do not send sensitive files or personal information you do not want shared with us. You can ask us to delete your message by emailing the same address.
privacy.pGithub: If you visit the <a:repo>{repoLink}</a:repo> or post an issue, GitHub handles that visit and anything you submit there under <a:privacy>{privacyLink}</a:privacy>. Issues are public, so do not include private data in them.
privacy.pChanges: We may update this policy if the site changes. The current version will appear on this page. For questions about your data, email <a:email>{emailLink}</a:email>.

compressPdf.leadStrong: Make a PDF easier to share.
compressPdf.lead: Choose a compression level, compare file sizes, and download the result. Your PDF stays in this browser.
compressPdf.caption: Free PDF compressor · No upload · No sign-up
compressPdf.howIntro: Choose or drop one PDF, select how to compress it, and click {button}. You will see the original size, output size and percentage saved before download. Files up to 30MB and 60 pages are supported. Processing happens in your browser.
compressPdf.howKeepTitle: Keep text or make a smaller file
compressPdf.howKeepP1: {keepText} rewrites the PDF structure. It preserves selectable text, links and forms, but often saves little space. {makeSmaller} renders each page as a JPEG image in a new PDF. This can reduce image-heavy and scanned PDFs substantially, but text can no longer be selected or searched, and links, forms, bookmarks and accessibility information are lost. Check the result before sharing it.
compressPdf.howKeepP2: Do not use either rewrite mode for a digitally signed PDF you need to keep valid. Any change to a signed file can invalidate its signature.
compressPdf.howLimitP: Use the maximum-size selector when a website asks for a file under 100KB, 200KB or 500KB. If needed, the tool tries progressively smaller image settings. A target cannot be guaranteed: page count and image detail set a practical minimum. The measured output and a clear target status are always shown. For a preselected limit, use <a:pdf100>{pdf100Label}</a:pdf100>, <a:pdf200>{pdf200Label}</a:pdf200> or <a:pdf500>{pdf500Label}</a:pdf500>.
compressPdf.faqA1: No. It is read and processed on your device.
compressPdf.faqQ2: Why did the file not get smaller?
compressPdf.faqA2: A PDF may already contain efficient images and compressed streams. This tool keeps the original if its alternatives would be larger.
compressPdf.faqQ3: Can I compress a password-protected PDF?
compressPdf.faqA3: No. Unlock it first in an app you trust, then choose the unlocked file.
compressPdf.target.leadStrong: Check whether your PDF can fit a {target}KB limit.
compressPdf.target.lead: Compress it in your browser, see the exact output size, and download it when it meets your needs.
compressPdf.target.caption: {target}KB = {bytes} bytes · No upload
compressPdf.target.howTitle: How to compress a PDF to {target}KB
compressPdf.target.howP1: Choose a PDF or drag it into the tool. The maximum size is already set to {target}KB. Click {button} and compare the measured result with the limit before downloading. If your PDF is already at or under {target}KB, the original is kept.
compressPdf.target.howP2: For a tight limit, the default mode rebuilds pages as compressed images. This removes selectable text, live links, forms, bookmarks and accessibility information. Switch to {keepText} if those features matter; that mode usually achieves a smaller reduction. Image-heavy scans tend to shrink more than text-only PDFs.
compressPdf.target.howP3: Not every PDF can reach {target}KB. More pages and detailed graphics need more data, and aggressive compression may make small text hard to read. The tool reports when it cannot reach the limit and never labels an oversized result as successful. Check legibility before submitting the file.
compressPdf.target.how100: For a 100KB form limit: a one-page PDF has a better chance than a long document. If the result is over 100KB or fine print becomes unreadable, reduce the source scan resolution or remove unneeded pages in your PDF editor before trying again.
compressPdf.target.how200: For a 200KB application upload: start with Balanced compression, then inspect names, dates and any small printed labels in the download. Choose Strong if size matters more than fine image detail.
compressPdf.target.how500: For a 500KB attachment: try Light compression to retain more visual detail. If your PDF already fits, this tool returns it unchanged. If selectable text matters, try Keep text and links and check whether that result fits.
compressPdf.target.howOther: Need another limit? Try <a:target1>{target1Label}</a:target1>, <a:target2>{target2Label}</a:target2>, or use the <a:main>{mainLabel}</a:main>. Files stay on your device.

imageResizer.lead: Set pixels, a percentage, centimetres or a maximum KB. Apply the same settings to a batch and download each result or one ZIP.

imageResizer.howTitle: How to resize or compress an image online
imageResizer.howSubtitle: Choose your images, set a size and download the results.
imageResizer.howIntro: Choose JPG, PNG or WebP images, or drop them on the tool. This online image resizer and compressor handles up to 20 photos at once. Each file can be up to 25MB. Processing happens in your browser, so your images are not uploaded.
imageResizer.howBatchTitle: Pixels, percentage and bulk image resizing
imageResizer.howBatchP: Enter a width and height in pixels, or scale each image by a percentage. With {lockAspect} on, the dimensions form a maximum-size box: each image fits inside it without being stretched. Turn it off to set exact width and height. {noEnlarge} prevents a smaller photo from being scaled up. Select {estimate} to check the first image before resizing; in a batch, each image may produce a different file size. For a batch, the same settings are applied to every image; choose individual downloads or a ZIP.
imageResizer.howCmP: Choose {cmMode} and enter the intended width, height and resolution in pixels per inch (PPI). The tool converts cm to pixel dimensions using pixels = cm ÷ 2.54 × PPI. For example, 5 cm at 300 PPI is about 591 pixels. The downloaded image does not have a print-size or DPI metadata setting, so set the same print resolution in your printing software.
imageResizer.howKbTitle: Compress an image to a target KB
imageResizer.howKbP: To use it as an image compressor, choose {kbMode} and enter a maximum. This mode saves a JPG, lowers its quality first and, only if needed, reduces its pixel dimensions until it fits. Transparent areas become white. Some detail may be lost at a small target size. A JPG already under the limit is kept as-is. Need a specific JPG limit? Use {jpg50Label} or {jpg100Label}.
imageResizer.howFormatsP: For pixel, percentage and cm resizing, save in the original format or choose JPG, PNG or WebP. JPG cannot keep transparency; transparent pixels are filled white. PNG can be larger than the original even when its dimensions shrink. Animated images and SVG are not supported. Resizing upward creates more pixels but cannot recover detail that was not in the original.
compressJpg.leadStrong: Make a JPG fit a {target}KB limit.
compressJpg.lead: Choose a photo, preview it, then download a JPG at or below {target}KB. The exact output size is shown before you save.
compressJpg.caption: Free JPG compressor · No upload · No sign-up
compressJpg.howP1: Choose one JPG or drop it on the tool. It searches for a high JPG quality that fits within {target}KB ({bytes} bytes). If reducing quality is not enough, it reduces the image dimensions and tries again. The result shows its pixel dimensions and {fileSizeText} before download.
compressJpg.howP2: If the original JPG is already {target}KB or less, you can download an unchanged copy. Compression may remove fine detail, especially in photos with text or complex patterns. A {target}KB limit may require a noticeably smaller image. Everything runs in your browser; the photo is not sent to a server.

qrScanner.lead: Use your camera, choose an image, or paste a screenshot. Review the decoded link or text before you act on it.
qrScanner.caption: Free online QR scanner · No sign-up · On-device decoding
qrScanner.howTitle: How to scan a QR code
qrScanner.howSubtitle: Your camera feed and images stay on your device.
qrScanner.howCameraP: The camera starts when you open this page. Allow camera access when prompted, then keep the full code in view until it is read. The camera stops after a successful scan. You can inspect and copy the full result, then choose whether to open a web link.
qrScanner.howImageP: Choose Image, then select or drop a PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF or BMP image. You can also paste a screenshot from your clipboard. For best results, use a clear, straight-on image with the entire QR code and its blank border visible.
qrScanner.howResultP1: The scanner shows the exact text encoded in the QR code. For web links, it also shows the destination and offers an explicit Open link button. It never opens a scanned link automatically. Only http:// and https:// addresses can be opened from the result. Scans are not saved or uploaded.
qrScanner.howResultP2: This online QR code scanner works in modern desktop and mobile browsers. Camera access needs a secure connection and your permission. If camera access is unavailable, scan a saved image instead. It reads QR codes, rather than other barcode types.
qrScanner.faqA1: Yes. There is no account, installation, or scan limit.
qrScanner.faqQ2: Can I scan a QR code from a screenshot?
qrScanner.faqA2: Yes. Choose an image or paste a screenshot into the image panel.
qrScanner.faqA3: No. Decoding happens in this browser tab. Camera access stops when you stop scanning, scan a code, switch to image mode, or leave the page.

csvJson.caption: CSV, TSV and text files up to 10 MB
csvJson.howIntro: Paste CSV or TSV, choose a local file, or drag one into the converter. It reads the file on your device and converts it in a browser worker. Nothing is uploaded. The output updates as you edit the input or settings.
csvJson.howFirstRowResult: Each following row becomes an object with those names as keys. Blank or repeated names get unique labels.
csvJson.howNoHeaderResult: Every row becomes an object with keys such as {col1} and {col2}.
csvJson.howValuesResult: Values stay strings by default, preserving codes and leading zeros. You can detect safe numbers and booleans or turn empty cells into null.

csvJson.howQuotesResult: It stays within one field. Double a quote inside a quoted field, as standard CSV requires.
csvJson.howSeparators: Auto detect checks comma, semicolon, tab and pipe separators. You can set one explicitly if the preview looks wrong. UTF-8, UTF-16 and Windows-1252 files are supported; set the encoding if characters look incorrect.
csvJson.howOutput: Pretty and compact output are JSON arrays. JSON Lines writes one object per line for tools that accept .jsonl. The preview shows at most eight rows and 25 columns; Copy JSON and Download include all rows and columns. Rows with fewer fields get empty values, and rows with extra fields get generated column names. The converter points out differing row widths and renamed headers.
csvJson.howLimits: Files are limited to 10 MB and 500 columns. Large conversions may use substantial memory on a phone. Need to explore or edit the table first? Open the <a:csvViewer>CSV viewer</a:csvViewer>. For the reverse conversion, use <a:jsonCsv>{jsonCsvLabel}</a:jsonCsv>.

csvViewer.lead: Search rows, filter a column, sort, fix cells and export the result. Everything runs locally in your browser.

csvViewer.howIntro: Choose a file, drop it on the viewer, or paste CSV text. The file is read and parsed in a browser worker; its contents are not sent to a server. Commas, semicolons, tabs and pipes are detected automatically. If the table looks wrong, set the separator in Import settings before opening the file.
csvViewer.howExploreP1: Search every column, filter one column by text, and click a heading to sort in either direction. The column details panel counts shown values, blanks and distinct values, with examples. Click a cell to change it. Revert edits restores the original values in this tab.
csvViewer.howExploreP2: The grid renders only rows near the visible area so large tables remain practical to scroll. Files are limited to 10 MB and 500 columns; very large datasets can still use substantial device memory. Rows with missing fields are padded with empty cells, and you can isolate rows whose field counts differ.
csvViewer.howSaveP1: Choose all rows or shown rows before downloading CSV or JSON, or copying tab-separated text. CSV downloads use commas and UTF-8. JSON values remain strings, so codes such as 001 are preserved. Your original file is never changed.
csvViewer.howSaveP2: UTF-8, UTF-16 and Windows-1252 file encodings are supported. Encoding detection uses byte marks and text checks; choose the encoding manually in Import settings if characters look wrong.

jsonBeautifier.howP1: The beautifier checks that your input is valid JSON, then adds line breaks and indentation. Choose 2 spaces, 4 spaces or tabs. Compact removes optional whitespace when you need a smaller text file. The output can be copied or downloaded as .json.
jsonBeautifier.howP2: Objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans and null are accepted at the top level. Integer digits larger than JavaScript can safely represent are preserved. As with JSON parsing generally, duplicate object keys collapse to their last value, and object keys made only of integer digits may be reordered.
jsonBeautifier.howP3: For invalid JSON, the message points to a line and column and suggests a fix for common problems such as trailing commas, single quotes and unquoted keys. JSON Lines, comments and JSON with trailing commas are not accepted as standard JSON. Files up to 10 MB are processed locally in a Web Worker; large files may use substantial memory on a phone.

csvSql.lead: Paste data or choose a file, select your database, then copy or download the generated SQL. Conversion happens in your browser.

Type detection recognizes booleans and conservative integer or decimal values; dates stay text because date formats vary by database.
csvSql.howLimits: The full result is available through Copy SQL or Download .sql. The on-page SQL preview shows its beginning when output is long, and the table preview shows the first 100 rows and 30 columns. Large files can take longer on a phone. For MySQL, backslashes are escaped using its usual string syntax; review that output if your server uses NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES.

dbfExcel.lead: Choose a DBF file, check the records and download an XLSX workbook. Everything runs in this browser.
dbfExcel.caption: .dbf to .xlsx · Up to 20 MB · No upload
dbfExcel.howTitle: How to convert DBF to Excel
dbfExcel.howIntro: Choose or drop a .dbf file. The converter reads its fields and records, creates an .xlsx workbook, and shows a preview before download. Each DBF field becomes a column; each active record becomes a row. Records marked as deleted are skipped.
dbfExcel.howTypesP: Text, numeric, date and logical fields become Excel text, numbers, dates and booleans. Long numbers that Excel would round are kept as text. The DBF header selects the text encoding when it has a recognized language marker. If names or values look wrong in the preview, choose a different encoding and convert again.
dbfExcel.howLimitsP: This tool reads common dBASE III, dBASE IV and FoxPro DBF tables up to 20 MB. A DBF with memo, picture or general fields needs companion files such as .dbt or .fpt; those fields are not converted here. Unrecognized field types and malformed tables produce an error instead of a partial spreadsheet. One worksheet can hold up to 1,048,575 data rows and 16,384 columns.
dbfExcel.faqA1: No. The tool generates a standard XLSX file in your browser. You can open it in Excel or another compatible spreadsheet app.
dbfExcel.faqA2: No. The file stays on your device during conversion.
dbfExcel.faqQ3: Can I get a legacy XLS file?
dbfExcel.faqA3: This converter downloads XLSX, the current Excel workbook format. It does not create the older XLS format.

xmlJson.howDetails: XML has attributes, namespaces, comments and mixed content; JSON has no single standard way to represent them. This converter keeps namespace prefixes in names and omits comments and processing instructions. Simple text and #text are trimmed; #content retains the spaces around inline elements. It rejects DOCTYPE declarations and malformed XML, with a line and column for syntax errors.

emlPdf.howBodyP: Paragraphs, headings, bold and italic text, lists, quoted replies, links, simple tables and images sent inside the email are kept. Newsletter layouts are simplified to one column, and colors and custom fonts are not copied. When a message has both a formatted and a plain-text version, you can choose which one to use. emlPdf.howAttachP: Attachments are listed in the header with their sizes. With {embed}, the files are also saved inside the PDF, where readers such as Adobe Acrobat Reader and Firefox show them in an attachments panel. Choose {list} for a smaller PDF that only names them.

emlPdf.faqQ3: Can I open the attachments from the PDF?

mhtPdf.description: Convert MHT to PDF online, free and with no upload. Turns .mht and .mhtml files into a PDF with the page’s text, links and saved images, or prints the page as it looks.
mhtPdf.leadStrong: Convert an MHT file to PDF.

mhtPdf.howTitle: How to convert MHT to PDF
mhtPdf.howIntro: Choose or drop an .mht or .mhtml file. The converter reads the web archive in your browser and builds a PDF that starts with the page title, the web address it was saved from and the date, followed by the page. Text in the PDF can be selected and searched, and links stay clickable. Choose {pageOnly} to leave the title and address out.
mhtPdf.howKeepsP: Headings, paragraphs, bold and italic text, lists, links, simple tables and the images saved inside the file are kept. The page is laid out in one column, top to bottom: its colors, fonts and side-by-side columns are not copied, and parts that the page’s style sheet hides, such as closed menus, may appear. Images that the page loaded from the internet but that weren’t saved in the file are not downloaded.
mhtPdf.howPrintP: {print} opens your browser’s print dialog with the page as it was saved, with its styles, columns and images. Choose Save as PDF as the destination to get a PDF that looks like the page. The text stays selectable. Scripts in the page don’t run and nothing is loaded from the internet, so images that weren’t saved in the file stay blank.
mhtPdf.whatP: An .mht or .mhtml file (MIME HTML) is a web page saved as one file: the page, its images and its style sheets are packed together in the same format email uses for attachments, defined in <a:rfc>RFC 2557</a:rfc>. Internet Explorer saved pages this way as “Web Archive, single file”, Chrome and Edge save them as “Webpage, Single File”, Word saves documents as a “Single File Web Page”, and Windows Steps Recorder saves its recordings as an .mht file inside a ZIP file.
mhtPdf.howLimitsP: This tool reads .mht and .mhtml files up to 50 MB, and the first .mht file inside a .zip file, such as a Steps Recorder recording. A plain HTML file renamed to .mht works too, without its images. Latin, Greek and Cyrillic text is supported in the PDF. Pages mostly in other scripts, such as Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Hebrew or Hindi, can’t be made into a PDF here yet, and emoji are left out; the print view can still save those pages as a PDF. For emails saved as .eml files, use EML to PDF.
mhtPdf.faqA1: No. The file is read and converted on your device. The page downloads a font from this site to build the PDF, but the saved page never leaves your browser.
mhtPdf.faqQ2: How do I open an MHT file without Internet Explorer?
mhtPdf.faqA2: Chrome and Edge open .mht and .mhtml files: drag the file into a browser window. Word opens them too. To keep a copy that opens anywhere, convert it to PDF here.
mhtPdf.faqQ3: How do I convert a Steps Recorder file to PDF?
mhtPdf.faqA3: Steps Recorder saves a ZIP file with an .mht file inside. Choose the ZIP file here, or the .mht file after unzipping it, and the recorded steps and the screenshots saved in the file go into the PDF.
mhtPdf.faqQ4: Can iLovePDF convert MHT to PDF?
mhtPdf.faqA4: iLovePDF’s HTML to PDF tool takes a web address, HTML, CSS or JS files, or a ZIP file of them, but it doesn’t list .mht or .mhtml files (checked in October 2026). This page converts .mht and .mhtml files directly, without uploading them.
mhtPdf.faqQ5: Why are some images missing from the PDF?
mhtPdf.faqA5: An .mht file holds only the images that were saved with the page. Images the page loaded from other sites, or that were added after the page was saved, may not be in the file. This tool doesn’t download them, so the website can’t tell that you opened the page.

webpPng.description: Convert WebP to PNG online for free, keeping transparency and every pixel. Convert one image, a batch or a ZIP file in your browser, with no upload.

webpPng.howTitle: How to convert WebP to PNG
webpPng.howIntro: Drop .webp files or a .zip of them onto the converter, or choose them from your device, then press {button}. Download each PNG, or all of them in one ZIP. Every PNG has the same width and height as its WebP, and the same name with a new extension: logo.webp becomes logo.png.
webpPng.howQualityTitle: Does converting to PNG lose quality?
webpPng.howQualityP: No. PNG is lossless, so the PNG shows exactly what the WebP shows, including transparent and semi-transparent areas. It can’t bring back detail that a lossy WebP already discarded, though. A PNG is often several times larger than the WebP, especially for photos. For photos where file size matters, <a:jpg>convert WebP to JPG</a:jpg> instead.
webpPng.howAnimatedP: A PNG holds a single image, so an animated WebP becomes a PNG of its first frame. To keep the animation, <a:gif>convert WebP to GIF</a:gif>. For JPG, GIF and SVG in one place, use the <a:hub>WebP converter</a:hub>.
webpPng.faqQ1: Why is my PNG bigger than the WebP?
webpPng.faqA1: WebP compresses images more efficiently than PNG. The PNG stores the same pixels in a less compact way, so a bigger file is expected and doesn’t mean anything went wrong.
webpPng.faqQ2: Can I convert many WebP images to PNG at once?
webpPng.faqA2: Yes. Choose up to 200 images, or a ZIP file that contains them, and download the PNG files in one ZIP. Folders inside your ZIP are kept.

webpJpg.howQualityP: {high} suits most photos: the difference from the original is hard to see and the file stays small. {max} keeps more fine detail for printing or further editing, and makes larger files. {small} makes the smallest files, for email and upload forms with a size limit, with some softening in fine detail.
webpJpg.howTransparencyP: JPG can’t store transparency. Transparent parts of a WebP, such as the background around a logo or sticker, are filled with white, or with black if you choose it. To keep them transparent, <a:png>convert WebP to PNG</a:png>.
webpJpg.howJpegP: They’re the same format. JPEG is the name of the standard, and .jpg is the shorter file extension that early versions of Windows needed. This converter saves files with the .jpg extension, which opens everywhere .jpeg does. For PNG, GIF and SVG in one place, use the <a:hub>WebP converter</a:hub>.
webpJpg.faqQ1: Does converting WebP to JPG lose quality?
webpJpg.faqA1: A little, because JPG compresses the image again. At Balanced or Best quality the difference is hard to see. An animated WebP keeps only its first frame; <a:gif>convert it to GIF</a:gif> to keep the animation.
webpJpg.faqQ2: Can I convert WebP to JPG in bulk?
webpJpg.faqA2: Yes. Choose up to 200 images at once, or a ZIP file that contains them, and download all the JPG files in one ZIP.

webpGif.description: Convert animated WebP to GIF online for free, keeping every frame and its timing. Still images work too, one at a time or in bulk, with no upload.

webpGif.howColorsP: A GIF can show at most 256 colors in each frame, so the converter picks the best 256 colors for every frame separately. Flat graphics and stickers look the same; photos and smooth gradients can show banding. For those, <a:png>convert WebP to PNG</a:png> instead. webpGif.howBrowserP: Reading every frame of an animated WebP needs the ImageDecoder feature, found in browsers such as Chrome and Edge. In a browser without it, an animated WebP becomes a still GIF of its first frame, and the converter tells you. Very long or very large animations are refused rather than left to slow your device down. For PNG, JPG and SVG in one place, use the <a:hub>WebP converter</a:hub>.
webpGif.faqQ1: Why is my GIF bigger than the WebP?
webpGif.faqA1: WebP compresses animation far more efficiently than GIF, a format from 1987. A GIF several times the size of the WebP is normal.
webpGif.faqQ2: Can I convert many WebP files to GIF at once?

webpSvg.howTypesTitle: Vector paths or an embedded image
webpSvg.howTraceP: {trace} turns areas of similar color into filled shapes. The SVG stays sharp at any size, and you can edit it in apps such as Illustrator, Inkscape, Figma and Cricut Design Space. It works best for logos, icons, text and flat drawings. Photos come out posterized, made of a few flat colors, and make large files.
webpSvg.howEmbedP: {embed} keeps every pixel by placing the image, as a PNG, inside the SVG file. It looks exactly like the WebP, but it’s still made of pixels: it doesn’t get sharper when enlarged, and cutting machines can’t cut it. Use it when a website or app only accepts SVG files.
webpSvg.howColorsP: The number of colors sets how many flat colors the tracing uses. 2 suits black-and-white logos, signatures and stencils, 8 or 16 suits most logos and icons, and 32 keeps more shading but makes a bigger file. Images larger than about 1 megapixel are traced at that size to keep tracing quick, and the SVG still displays at the original size. An animated WebP is converted from its first frame.
webpSvg.faqQ1: Is the SVG a real vector file?
webpSvg.faqA1: With {trace}, yes: the file contains only shapes and no pixels. With {embed}, no: it’s an SVG file that contains the original pixels.
webpSvg.faqQ2: Why does my traced photo look posterized?
webpSvg.faqA2: Tracing turns an image into a limited number of flat colors. That suits logos and drawings, but a photo’s smooth shading can’t be made from a few shapes. Choose 32 colors for more detail, or <a:png>convert the photo to PNG</a:png> or <a:jpg>JPG</a:jpg> instead.
webp.faqUploadA: No. Your browser reads and converts the images on your device, and nothing is sent to a server, so the converter is also safe to use for private photos and screenshots.

They’re listed by file name, so IMG_2.jpg comes before IMG_10.jpg; use the arrows to change the order, and {add} to bring in more. Pick {image} or {pdf} under {outputLabel}, then press the merge button and download the result.
mergeJpg.howLayoutTitle: Top to bottom, side by side or a grid
mergeJpg.howLayoutP: {vertical} stacks the images into one long image, like a screenshot of a long chat or web page. {horizontal} puts them in a row, for a before-and-after picture. {grid} makes rows of 2, 3 or 4 images, for a collage or a contact sheet. With {match}, every image is scaled to the width of the narrowest one (or, side by side, the height of the lowest one), so nothing is enlarged and nothing looks blurry. {original} keeps each image’s own size and fills the space around smaller ones with the background color.
mergeJpg.howQualityP: The merged image is saved as a new JPG at the quality you choose. {high} looks like the originals and keeps the file small. Browsers can’t make an image larger than 16,384 pixels on a side or 50 megapixels in total, so a very long merge is made smaller to fit, and the page says so. To keep every pixel of every photo, merge them into a PDF instead: each JPG goes into the PDF unchanged.
mergeJpg.howPdfP: Choose {pdf} to put each image on its own page, in the order of the list. The Merge JPG to PDF page explains the page size, orientation and margin options.
mergeJpg.howJpegP: JPG and JPEG are the same format with two spellings of the file extension, so .jpg and .jpeg files merge together, and the result opens anywhere either one does. PNG and WebP images can be added too. Phone photos are turned the right way up using their orientation tag, and iPhone photos arrive as JPG when you choose them from the photo library.
mergeJpg.faqQ1: Is it free to merge JPG files here?
mergeJpg.faqA1: Yes. There’s no sign-up, no watermark and no daily limit. You can merge up to 100 images at a time, 50 MB each.
mergeJpg.faqQ2: Can I merge JPG to JPEG?
mergeJpg.faqA2: Yes. They’re the same format, so merging JPG files gives you a JPEG too; only the extension is spelled differently. The merged file is saved as .jpg, which opens in every app that opens .jpeg.

mergeJpgPdf.howPageP: {a4} and {letter} are paper sizes for printing and for upload forms; each image is scaled to fill the page inside the margins, and centered. With {auto} orientation, wide images get landscape pages and tall ones portrait pages. {small} margins are half an inch (13 mm) and {large} margins an inch (25 mm). {fit} makes each page exactly the size of its image, at 96 pixels per inch, with no white border.

To make it smaller for an upload limit, run it through <a:compress>Compress PDF</a:compress> afterwards. PNG and WebP images, and JPGs in the CMYK colors some printers use, are saved as high-quality JPG before they go in.
mergeJpgPdf.howScanP: Merging is a quick way to make one PDF from photos of a document’s pages, receipts for an expense claim, or scans for a job or visa application. Phone photos are turned the right way up using their orientation tag. To combine several images into one image, without pages, use <a:hub>Merge JPG</a:hub>.

mergeJpgPdf.faqA1: Choose the JPG files, put them in the order you want the pages, pick a page size and press {button}. Each image becomes one page of the PDF.
mergeJpgPdf.faqQ2: Will the PDF be smaller than my images?
mergeJpgPdf.faqA2: No, it’s about the same size, because the JPG data goes in unchanged. To shrink it, use <a:compress>Compress PDF</a:compress>, which can turn each page into a smaller JPEG.

videoGif.description: Convert video to GIF online for free. Turn an MP4, MOV or WebM clip into an animated GIF: choose the start and end, the size, frame rate and speed. No upload.
videoGif.leadStrong: Turn a video into an animated GIF.
videoGif.lead: Choose an MP4, MOV or WebM video, pick the part you want, and set the size, frame rate and speed. The video never leaves this browser, so there’s no upload to wait for.
videoGif.caption: MP4, MOV, WebM and more, up to 2 GB, no upload
videoGif.howTitle: How to make a GIF from a video
videoGif.howIntro: Drop a video on the converter or choose one from your device. Play it to find the moment you want, then press {startHere} and {endHere}, or type the times. Choose a width, frame rate, speed and loop, then press {button}. The GIF appears under the video, ready to download.
videoGif.howSettingsTitle: Choosing the size and frame rate
videoGif.howSettingsP: A GIF stores every frame as a picture with at most 256 colors, so it grows quickly with the width, the frame rate and the length. 480 pixels at 10 frames per second suits chats and documents. 15 or 20 frames per second makes fast motion smoother, and 320 pixels or 5 frames per second keeps a long clip small. Speed changes how fast the GIF plays, not how many frames it has. The converter never makes a GIF wider than the video.
videoGif.howFormatsP: The converter reads frames with your browser’s own video player, so it takes any video the browser can play. MP4 (H.264) and WebM play in every current browser. MOV files and iPhone videos in HEVC (H.265) play in Safari, and in Chrome and Edge on most recent devices. AVI, WMV and FLV files usually don’t play in browsers; convert them to MP4 first. A GIF can have up to 1,000 frames, so a long part needs a lower frame rate.
videoGif.howYoutubeTitle: Making a GIF from a YouTube video
videoGif.howYoutubeP: The converter works with video files on your device; it can’t open a YouTube link. If the video is yours, <a:studio>download it from YouTube Studio</a:studio> (Content, then the menu next to the video, then Download) and choose the MP4 here. For someone else’s video, <a:terms>YouTube’s terms</a:terms> only allow downloading where YouTube offers it, so ask the creator for the file, and only share GIFs of clips you have the right to use.
videoGif.howPhoneP: On iPhone and Android, {choose} opens your photo library or files, and screen recordings work too. Reading frames from a long 4K video takes memory and time; if the converter stops, choose a smaller width or a shorter part.
videoGif.howGifP: GIF is an image format from 1987 that almost every app, browser and email program shows, always without sound. That’s why it’s used for reactions, short loops and how-to clips in documents. It’s far larger than a video of the same clip, so keep the MP4 for anything long. To turn an animated WebP into a GIF, use <a:webp>WebP to GIF</a:webp>.
videoGif.faqQ1: How long can the GIF be?
videoGif.faqA1: Up to 1,000 frames, and fewer at large widths: 100 seconds at 10 frames per second, or 40 seconds at 25. The video itself can be up to 2 GB and any length, since you choose the part to convert.
videoGif.faqA2: No. GIF images can’t hold sound, so the audio is left out.
videoGif.faqQ3: Why is the GIF bigger than the video?
videoGif.faqA3: A video stores mostly what changes between frames; a GIF stores each frame almost whole, with up to 256 colors. A GIF several times the size of the MP4 is normal. A smaller width, a lower frame rate or a shorter part makes it smaller.
videoGif.faqA4: No. Your browser reads the video and makes the GIF on your device, and nothing is sent to a server, so it’s safe for private clips and screen recordings.
videoGif.faqQ5: What frame rate should a GIF have?
videoGif.faqA5: 10 to 15 frames per second looks smooth for most clips. Browsers show GIF frames shorter than 20 milliseconds at 100 milliseconds, which slows the GIF down, so the converter stops at 25 frames per second.

wordCounter.howIntro: Everything is counted in this browser tab as you type, and nothing is sent anywhere. The text is gone when you close the tab.
wordCounter.howWordsP1: A word is anything between spaces that contains a letter or a digit. Contractions like don't and hyphenated words like well-known count as one word, while a dash or an ampersand on its own isn't a word. Chinese, Japanese and Thai are written without spaces, so for those the browser's built-in dictionary finds where each word ends.
wordCounter.howWordsP2: Word processors and websites don't all follow the same rules, so another counter can differ by a few words, mostly around dashes, slashes and numbers. When a form or an application sets a word limit, its own counter is the one that decides.
wordCounter.howCharsP1: Characters counts everything in the box, including spaces and line breaks. Characters without spaces leaves out spaces, tabs and line breaks. Letters counts letters only, so digits, punctuation and emoji are left out.
wordCounter.howCharsP2: A character is counted the way you see it: é, 👍🏽 and 🇯🇵 are one character each. Some websites and databases count the code units underneath instead, and there a single emoji can use up 2 or more characters of a limit.
wordCounter.howSentencesP: A sentence ends with a full stop, a question mark or an exclamation mark, or at the end of a line, so a heading on its own line counts as one. An abbreviation followed by a capital letter, as in “Dr. Smith”, is counted as the end of a sentence. A paragraph is a line with text on it, and the blank lines between paragraphs don't count. Lines counts every line up to the last one with text, blank lines included.
wordCounter.howTimeP: Reading time assumes 238 words a minute and speaking time 183 words a minute: the averages for silent reading of non-fiction and for reading aloud in <a:study>a 2019 review of 190 studies</a:study> by Marc Brysbaert. Chinese and Japanese are timed by character instead, at 500 characters a minute for reading and 300 for speaking. People read at very different speeds, so treat both times as a rough guide.
wordCounter.howTopP: Top words lists the words you use most, how many times each one appears and its share of all your words, which SEO tools call keyword density. Choose 2-word or 3-word phrases to find phrases you repeat. Common words such as “the”, “and” and “of” are skipped, along with phrases that start or end with one; untick the box to include them. Capital letters are ignored, so “Apple” and “apple” count as the same word.
wordCounter.howLimitP: Enter a limit to see how many characters or words you have left, for example for a meta description, a text message, a social media post or an application essay. You can open .txt and .md files up to 5 MB. For a Word document or a PDF, copy the text and paste it in. Long texts are counted in the background, so typing stays smooth.
wordCounter.faqQ1: Does the character count include spaces?
wordCounter.faqA1: Yes. Characters includes spaces and line breaks, because most forms and websites count them. Characters without spaces is shown next to it for limits that leave spaces out.
wordCounter.faqQ2: Does it work for other languages?
wordCounter.faqA2: Yes. Every character counts once in any script, including accented letters, Cyrillic, Arabic, Korean and Chinese. Common words are skipped in the top words list only for the language of this page.

tip.description: Work out the tip and total in seconds. Pick 15%, 18%, 20% or any tip, tip before or after tax, split the bill and round up each share. With a US tipping guide by service.
tip.leadStrong: Enter the bill to see the tip and the total.
tip.lead: Pick a tip or type your own, split it between people, tip on the amount before tax and round up each share. The answer updates as you type, in your currency.
tip.caption: Restaurants, delivery, salons, taxis and any other bill, in 27 currencies
tip.howFormula: Tip = bill × tip percentage ÷ 100. For a 20% tip on a $48.50 bill, 48.50 × 20 ÷ 100 = $9.70, so you pay $58.20 in all. To split it, divide the total by the number of people: $29.10 each for two.
tip.howMental: To work it out in your head, start with 10%: move the decimal point one place to the left, so 10% of $48.50 is $4.85. Double that for 20% ($9.70). For 15%, add half of the 10% again: $4.85 + $2.43 = $7.28.
tip.howPhoneTitle: How to figure out a tip on a phone calculator
tip.howPhoneP1: The way that works on every calculator is to multiply. For a 20% tip, type the bill, then × 0.2 = to get the tip, or × 1.2 = to get the total with the tip included. For 15% use 0.15 and 1.15; for 18% use 0.18 and 1.18.
tip.howPhoneP2: The percent key works too, but not the same way on every calculator. On an iPhone, 48.50 + 20 % = gives the total, 58.2, as Apple's Calculator guide describes. Android calculators vary: some work the same way, while others read 20 % as 0.2 and show 48.7. If you're not sure, try 100 + 20 % = once. A calculator that shows 120 adds the tip for you.
tip.howTaxTitle: Should you tip before or after tax?
tip.howTaxP: The Emily Post Institute suggests tipping on the amount before tax. Choose “The bill before tax”, enter the tax from the receipt, and the tip is worked out on the rest. Tipping on the whole bill is simpler and gives a little more: on a $100 meal with 8% tax, a 20% tip is $20 before tax or $21.60 after.
tip.howSplitTitle: Splitting the bill and rounding up
tip.howSplitP: Enter the number of people to see what each person pays, tip included. Shares are rounded up to the cent, so together they always cover the bill: $100 split three ways is $33.34 each. To make paying easier, round each share up to $1, $5 or $10. The calculator shows how much rounding adds and what the tip comes to with it.

tip.guide.restaurant.note: Of the bill before tax, for table service. 10% at a buffet.
tip.guide.bar.note: A dollar or two per drink, or 15–20% when you run a tab.
tip.guide.takeout.note: No obligation. Up to 10% for curbside service or a large, complicated order.
tip.guide.delivery.note: Emily Post suggests 10–15% ($2–5 for pizza), NerdWallet at least 15%. DoorDash says Dashers receive 100% of customer tips.
tip.guide.grocery.note: NerdWallet suggests at least 15%. Instacart says 100% of the tip goes to the shopper.

tip.guide.hair.note: Ask for it to be split among everyone who served you.
tip.guide.nails.note: Of the price of the manicure or pedicure.
tip.guide.tattoo.note: Artists quoted by U.S. News suggest 15–20% or 20–25%, so $75–125 on a $500 tattoo.
tip.guide.rideshare.note: Of the fare. In a taxi, $2 for the first bag the driver carries and $1 for each one after.
tip.guide.movers.note: Usually a flat amount per mover, or $5–10 per mover per hour. Some guides suggest 15–20% of the moving bill.

tip.faqQ1: How much should I tip at a restaurant?
tip.faqA1: The Emily Post Institute suggests 15–20% of the bill before tax for table service in the US, and some guides now suggest 20% or more. The calculator starts at {default}.
tip.faqQ2: How much should I tip for takeout?
tip.faqA2: There's no obligation. The Emily Post Institute suggests a dollar or two, or up to 10% for a large, complicated order or curbside service.
tip.faqQ3: How much should I tip on DoorDash and other delivery apps?
tip.faqA3: Usually 10–20% of the order. The Emily Post Institute suggests 10–15%, and NerdWallet at least 15%. You add the tip in the app, and DoorDash says Dashers receive 100% of customer tips.
tip.faqQ4: How much should I tip movers?
tip.faqA4: Movers usually get a flat amount rather than a percentage. Reader's Digest suggests $20–50 per mover, or $5–10 per mover per hour; some guides suggest 15–20% of the moving bill instead.
tip.faqQ5: How much do you tip at a nail salon or for a tattoo?
tip.faqA5: 15–20% of the price at a nail or hair salon. For a tattoo, artists quoted by U.S. News suggest 15–25%, or $75–125 on a $500 tattoo. Enter the price as the bill and pick a tip.
tip.faqQ6: Do people tip in other countries?
tip.faqA6: Customs differ. Tipping isn't customary in Japan. In much of Europe, service is included in the price and people round up or leave a little extra, and in the UK many restaurants add an optional 12.5% service charge. Check the bill for a service charge before you add a tip.

hsGpa.howTitle: How to calculate your high school GPA
hsGpa.howStep1: Turn each grade into points. On the 4.0 scale an A is 4, a B 3, a C 2, a D 1 and an F 0. A plus adds 0.3 and a minus takes off 0.3, so a B+ is 3.3 and an A- is 3.7. Percentages become letters first: 93% is an A and 88% a B+.
hsGpa.howStep2: Add up the points and divide by the number of classes. That's your unweighted GPA. Grades of A, B+, B and A- give 4 + 3.3 + 3 + 3.7 = 14 points, and 14 ÷ 4 = 3.5.
hsGpa.howWeightedP: An unweighted GPA treats every class the same and tops out at 4.0. A weighted GPA gives harder classes extra points, most often 0.5 for honors and 1 for AP, IB and college (dual enrollment) classes, so an A in an AP class counts as 5. In the example above, if the B+ is an honors class and the A- is AP, the weighted GPA is (4 + 3.8 + 3 + 4.7) ÷ 4 = 3.88. An F earns 0 points in any class.
hsGpa.howCreditsP: Many high schools count every class the same, so you can calculate your GPA without credits: keep “Count every class the same” selected. If your school gives classes different credits, such as 0.5 for a one-semester class, choose “Use credits”. Each grade's points are then multiplied by the class's credits, and the total is divided by the total credits.
hsGpa.howCumulativeP: To combine this term with earlier ones, choose “Yes” under “Add a GPA from earlier terms” and enter your GPA so far and how many classes it covers. Each part counts in proportion to its classes: a 3.0 over 12 classes and a 3.5 over 4 new classes give (3.0 × 12 + 3.5 × 4) ÷ 16 = 3.13.
hsGpa.scaleIntro: Letter grades, percentages and grade points on the 4.0 scale.
hsGpa.scaleNotCounted: Earns credit, not part of the GPA
hsGpa.scaleNote: The percentages follow the common 10-point scale with plus and minus grades. <a:bigfuture>BigFuture</a:bigfuture>, from the College Board, gives the same points for whole letters (A 4.0, B 3.0, C 2.0, D 1.0) and notes that some schools use other cutoffs or no plus and minus grades. Checked September 2026. Your school's handbook has its own scale.
hsGpa.faqQ1: What is a good high school GPA?
hsGpa.faqA1: It depends on the colleges you're applying to. For comparison, the average US high school graduate in 2019 had a 3.11 GPA, according to the <a:hsts>NAEP High School Transcript Study</a:hsts>. A 3.0 is a B average and a 3.7 an A- average.
hsGpa.faqQ2: How do I calculate my GPA without credits?
hsGpa.faqA2: Give every class the same weight: turn each grade into points, add them up and divide by the number of classes. The calculator works this way unless you choose “Use credits”.
hsGpa.faqQ3: Can a GPA be higher than 4.0?
hsGpa.faqA3: An unweighted GPA can't go above 4.0, or 4.3 at schools where an A+ is worth 4.3. A weighted GPA can, because honors and AP classes earn extra points: straight A's in AP classes give a 5.0.
hsGpa.faqQ4: Do colleges look at weighted or unweighted GPA?
hsGpa.faqA4: Schools report GPAs in different ways, so colleges often recalculate them. <a:bigfuture>BigFuture</a:bigfuture> notes that colleges may adjust or remove the weighting for AP and honors classes to compare applicants from different schools. It helps to know both numbers.
hsGpa.faqQ5: How do I convert a percentage to a GPA?
hsGpa.faqA5: Find the letter for the percentage in the scale above, then its points: 85% is a B, worth 3.0. To convert a whole report card, choose “Percentages” and type each grade. The calculator shows the letter next to each one.
hsGpa.faqQ6: Do pass/fail classes and PE count?
hsGpa.faqA6: Pass/fail classes usually earn credit but aren't part of the GPA, so choose P (pass/fail) for them. Whether PE, electives and other non-core classes count depends on your school, so check its handbook.

gpa.howTitle: How to calculate your college GPA
gpa.howStep1: Turn each grade into points on the 4.0 scale. An A is 4, a B 3, a C 2, a D 1 and an F 0. At most colleges a plus adds 0.3 and a minus takes off 0.3, so a B+ is 3.3 and an A- is 3.7.
gpa.howStep2: Multiply each grade's points by the course's credits. These are quality points: a B+ in a 4-credit course is 3.3 × 4 = 13.2.
gpa.howStep3: Add up the quality points and divide by the credits. An A (3 credits), B+ (4), B (3) and A- (2) give 12 + 13.2 + 9 + 7.4 = 41.6 quality points over 12 credits, and 41.6 ÷ 12 = 3.47.
gpa.howRules: Registrars such as <a:stanford>Stanford</a:stanford> and <a:rowan>Rowan University</a:rowan> describe the same method. Pass/fail courses and withdrawals (W) aren't part of the GPA, but an F is: its credits count with 0 points.
gpa.howSemesterP: Your semester GPA covers one term. Your cumulative GPA covers every term so far, and it comes from all the quality points and credits together, not from averaging the semester GPAs: a 3.5 over 6 credits and a 2.0 over 3 credits make a 3.0, not a 2.75. Add a semester for each term, or enter your GPA so far and the credits behind it. A 3.2 over 60 credits and a 3.8 over 15 new credits give (3.2 × 60 + 3.8 × 15) ÷ 75 = 3.32.
gpa.howPlanP: To find the average you need for the rest of your degree, enter the GPA you want and the credits you still have to take. The calculator works out (target × all credits − quality points so far) ÷ credits left. With a 3.2 over 60 credits and 60 to go, finishing with a 3.5 takes a 3.8 average: (3.5 × 120 − 192) ÷ 60 = 3.8. The more credits you've taken, the less each new grade moves your GPA, so it pays to plan early.
gpa.howHonorsTitle: Cum laude, magna cum laude and summa cum laude
gpa.howHonorsP: Many colleges award Latin honors at graduation based on GPA. The <a:utah>University of Utah</a:utah> uses 3.5 for cum laude, 3.7 for magna cum laude and 3.9 for summa cum laude, and the calculator compares your GPA with those. Other colleges set higher or lower cutoffs, or honor a share of the class instead, such as the top 5%. The <a:guide>guide to cum laude</a:guide> compares several colleges.
gpa.scaleIntro: Letter grades, percentages and grade points for a college GPA.
gpa.scaleNote: The percentages follow the common 10-point scale, and each course's syllabus sets its own. Some colleges count plus and minus grades in thirds, such as <a:american>American University</a:american> (B+ 3.33, A- 3.67), and some have no A+ or no D-. Checked September 2026.
gpa.faqA1: It depends on the college. A common set is 3.5 for cum laude, 3.7 for magna cum laude and 3.9 for summa cum laude, used by the <a:utah>University of Utah</a:utah>. The <a:usc>University of South Carolina</a:usc> asks for 3.5, 3.75 and 3.95, and <a:ccny>City College of New York</a:ccny> for 3.2, 3.5 and 3.8. <a:utd>UT Dallas</a:utd> instead honors the top 5%, the next 10% and the next 15% of graduates.
gpa.faqA2: Not usually. Colleges weight each grade by its credits, but they don't add extra points for harder courses the way many high schools do for honors and AP classes. For a high school GPA, use the <a:hs>high school GPA calculator</a:hs>.
gpa.faqQ3: Do pass/fail and withdrawn courses count?
gpa.faqA3: A pass (P) or a withdrawal (W) earns no grade points and isn't part of the GPA at colleges such as <a:rowan>Rowan</a:rowan> and <a:stanford>Stanford</a:stanford>, so choose P or W for them. An F does count: its credits stay in the total with 0 points. Rules for a failed pass/fail course differ, so check your college's grading policy.
gpa.faqQ4: What happens to my GPA if I retake a course?
gpa.faqA4: At many colleges the new grade replaces the old one in the GPA, although both stay on the transcript. <a:ilstu>Illinois State University</a:ilstu> works this way. Other colleges average both attempts or only replace low grades. If yours replaces grades, enter just the new grade, and take the old course out of your GPA so far.
gpa.faqQ5: How do I convert a percentage to a 4.0 GPA?
gpa.faqA5: Find the letter grade for the percentage, then the letter's points: 85% is a B, worth 3.0, and 91% is an A-, worth 3.7. To convert a whole semester, choose “Percentages” and type each grade; the calculator shows the letter next to each one. A GPA from another country's scale needs that country's conversion table, not a formula.
gpa.faqQ6: Can a college GPA be higher than 4.0?
gpa.faqA6: Only where an A+ is worth more than an A. At <a:stanford>Stanford</a:stanford> it's 4.3, so choose 4.3 under “An A+ counts as” if your college does the same. Elsewhere an A+ counts as 4.0, and 4.0 is the highest GPA.

autoLoan.howTitle: How to calculate a car payment
autoLoan.howFormula: Monthly payment = P × r ÷ (1 − (1 + r)^−n), where P is the amount you borrow, r is the annual interest rate divided by 12, and n is the number of monthly payments. For $30,000 at 6% over 60 months, r is 0.005 and the payment is $579.98. Over the 60 payments you pay $4,799.09 in interest.
autoLoan.howAmount: The amount you borrow is the price, minus your down payment and your trade-in's value, plus anything you still owe on the trade-in, plus the sales tax and fees if you put them in the loan.
autoLoan.howSimple: Most car loans charge <a:cfpbSimple>simple interest</a:cfpbSimple>: each month's interest is worked out on the balance you still owe. As the balance falls, less of each payment goes to interest and more to principal, as the schedule shows. A lender that counts interest by the day can differ from it by a few dollars.
autoLoan.howTaxTitle: Sales tax, fees and your trade-in
autoLoan.howTaxP: Most states charge sales tax on the price minus your trade-in. Some tax the full price, including <a:cdtfa>California</a:cdtfa> and <a:vadmv>Virginia</a:vadmv>; choose “The full price” there. <a:oregon>Oregon</a:oregon> has no sales tax, but new cars sold by Oregon dealers carry a 0.5% vehicle privilege tax. Check the rate with your state's DMV or the dealer, and add the title, registration and documentation fees from the buyer's order.
autoLoan.howNegativeTitle: If you owe more than your trade-in is worth
autoLoan.howNegativeP: The difference, called negative equity, is added to the new loan, so you pay interest on it too. Enter the trade-in's value and what you still owe, and the calculator includes it.
autoLoan.howTermTitle: Longer terms: a lower payment, more interest
autoLoan.howTermP: The table under the calculator shows the same loan over 36 to 84 months. <a:cfpbTerms>A longer loan lowers the payment, but you pay more interest</a:cfpbTerms> and are more likely to owe more than the car is worth. At 6%, $30,000 over 84 months is $438.26 a month and $6,813.47 in interest. Edmunds found that 23.9% of new-car buyers in the second quarter of 2026 took loans of 84 months or longer.
autoLoan.howRefiP: Choose “Refinancing” and enter what you owe, your payment and your rate. The calculator works out how many payments you have left, then compares the rest of your current loan with the new one, fees included. A lower rate can save money once fees and the new term are counted. A longer term can lower the payment but cost more in all, and the result says so.

autoLoan.downTitle: How much down payment for a car
autoLoan.downP1: <a:experianDown>Experian suggests</a:experianDown> putting down at least 20% on a new car and at least 10% on a used one, and <a:kbb>Kelley Blue Book</a:kbb> calls 20% standard. A bigger down payment lowers the payment and the interest, and makes it less likely that you'll owe more than the car is worth as it loses value.
autoLoan.downP2: Many buyers put down less. Edmunds found the average down payment in the second quarter of 2026 was $5,815 on a new car, 11.6% of the price, and $4,016 on a used car. Use the 10% and 20% buttons to see what each does to your payment.
autoLoan.downP3: A common rule of thumb, 20/4/10, is 20% down, a loan of 4 years or less, and car costs under 10% of your monthly income. <a:experianIncome>Experian</a:experianIncome> puts that last part at 10% to 15%. It's a guide, not a rule that lenders use.
autoLoan.faqQ1: How do I calculate my car payment?
autoLoan.faqA1: Enter the price, your down payment, the loan term and the interest rate in the calculator. It works out the loan amount, then the monthly payment with the standard amortization formula, and shows the interest and total cost. Add sales tax, fees and a trade-in for a closer estimate.
autoLoan.faqQ2: What is the average car payment?
autoLoan.faqA2: $765 a month for a new car and $542 for a used car in the second quarter of 2026, according to Experian. The average new-car loan was $43,610 over 69.5 months, at an average APR of 6.35%.
autoLoan.faqQ3: How much should I put down on a car?
autoLoan.faqA3: Experian suggests at least 20% on a new car and 10% on a used car. On a $35,000 new car that's $7,000. If you put down less, the payment and interest are higher, and you're more likely to owe more than the car is worth.
autoLoan.faqQ4: Can you use a credit card for a down payment on a car?
autoLoan.faqA4: Often, if the dealer agrees. <a:experianCard>Experian</a:experianCard> says some dealers cap how much you can charge because they pay card processing fees, and some don't take cards for large amounts at all. A big charge raises your credit utilization, which can lower your score, and card rates are far higher than auto loan rates, so it only makes sense if you can pay the card off right away. A cash advance or convenience check usually costs a 3% to 5% fee and starts charging interest at once.
autoLoan.faqQ5: What's a good interest rate for a used car loan?
autoLoan.faqA5: The average APR on a used car loan was 11.19% in the second quarter of 2026, against 6.35% for a new car, according to Experian. With a credit score from 781 to 850 it averaged 6.29%, and from 501 to 600, 19.10%. Choose a used-car rate in the calculator's list to start from it.
autoLoan.faqQ6: Is it worth refinancing a car loan?
autoLoan.faqA6: It can be, if you get a lower rate. Experian found the average refinanced loan in the second quarter of 2026 had a rate of 7.97%, down from 10.40% on the original loans. The <a:cfpbRefi>CFPB</a:cfpbRefi> warns that stretching the term lowers the payment but can mean more interest, and that <a:cfpbPrepay>your current loan may have a prepayment penalty</a:cfpbPrepay>. Choose “Refinancing” above to compare, fees included.

overtime.errTooManyHours.week: A week has only {max} hours. Lower the hours.

overtime.errNoRegular: Enter the hours your salary pays for.
overtime.howFormula: Overtime pay = hourly rate × overtime rate × overtime hours. At $20 an hour, time and a half is $20 × 1.5 = $30 an hour, so 10 overtime hours pay $300. Add your regular pay for the total: 40 hours × $20 = $800, plus $300, is $1,100 for the week.
overtime.howRateTitle: How to calculate your overtime rate per hour
overtime.howRateP: Multiply your regular rate by the overtime multiplier: 1.5 for time and a half, 2 for double time. Under US law the regular rate is your pay for the week, leaving out the overtime premium and payments such as gifts, divided by all the hours you worked. So a shift differential or a promised bonus raises it. A $100 production bonus in a 50-hour week at $20 adds $2, making the regular rate $22 and the overtime rate $33. <a:bonuses>The Department of Labor explains bonuses</a:bonuses>.
overtime.howSalaryP: If you're salaried but not exempt, divide the salary for the week by the hours it's meant to pay for. $52,000 a year is $1,000 a week; for 40 hours that's $25 an hour, so overtime is $37.50 an hour. A monthly salary becomes a weekly one when you multiply it by 12 and divide by 52, <a:cfr>as the federal rules do</a:cfr>.
overtime.howDoubleTitle: Time and a half and double time
overtime.howDoubleP: Time and a half is 1.5 times your regular rate, the federal minimum for hours over 40 in a workweek. Double time is 2 times. It's required in a few places, such as <a:ca>California for hours over 12 in a day</a:ca>, and some employers pay it on holidays. Enter double-time hours under Double time and bonuses to add them.
overtime.tableIntro: The overtime rate per hour at common hourly rates, and what 10 hours of overtime pay.
overtime.rulesP1: Under the <a:flsa>Fair Labor Standards Act</a:flsa>, most hourly workers, and salaried workers paid less than {threshold} a week, must get at least time and a half for every hour over 40 in a workweek. Each week stands alone: hours aren't averaged over two weeks, and federal law doesn't require extra pay for weekends, holidays or long days.
overtime.rulesP2: Exempt employees, paid a salary of at least {threshold} a week for executive, administrative or professional work, aren't owed overtime. The duties decide it, not the job title. <a:exempt>See the salary levels</a:exempt>.
overtime.rulesP3: States can require more. California pays time and a half after 8 hours in a day and double time after 12, and a few other states, such as Alaska and Colorado, also count long days. When state and federal law differ, you get whichever pays more. <a:fs23>The Department of Labor's fact sheet</a:fs23> covers the federal rules.
overtime.countriesIntro: The calculator works with any rate. These are the minimums the law sets, checked in October 2026; a contract can pay more.
overtime.rules.US: At least 1.5× for hours over 40 in a workweek. Some states also pay for long days.
overtime.rules.MX: 2× for the first 9 overtime hours in a week, 3× after that.
overtime.rules.BR: At least +50% (1.5×) on the normal hourly pay.
overtime.rules.FR: +25% for the 36th to 43rd hour of the week, +50% after that. A collective agreement can set another rate of at least +10%.
overtime.rules.DE: No premium set by law. The employment contract or collective agreement sets it, or the hours are given back as time off.
overtime.rules.ES: Set by the collective agreement or contract, never less than the normal hourly pay, or given back as rest within 4 months.
overtime.rules.JP: +25% over 8 hours a day or 40 a week, +50% over 60 overtime hours a month, +35% on statutory days off, and +25% more late at night.
overtime.faqA1: In the US it's at least 1.5 times your regular rate for each hour over 40 in a workweek. At $15 an hour that's $22.50 an hour, at $20 it's $30, and at $25 it's $37.50. Some states and employers pay double time, 2 times the rate, for some hours.
overtime.faqQ2: How do I calculate overtime pay?
overtime.faqA2: Multiply your hourly rate by 1.5, then by your overtime hours. For 8 overtime hours at $18 an hour: $18 × 1.5 = $27, and $27 × 8 = $216. Add it to your regular pay for the week's total.
overtime.faqA3: No. Overtime is taxed at the same rates as the rest of your pay. A bigger paycheck can have more tax withheld, because payroll treats it as if you earned that much every pay period, but any extra is settled when you file your return. From 2025 to 2028, the no tax on overtime deduction can lower the tax on part of it.
overtime.faqQ4: Do I get overtime for working over 8 hours a day?
overtime.faqA4: Not under federal law, which counts only hours over 40 in a workweek. California and a few other states pay overtime for long days, and some contracts do too. Enter those hours as overtime in the calculator.
overtime.faqQ5: How do I calculate overtime for a month?
overtime.faqA5: Choose A month and enter the month's hours. With a monthly salary, the calculator divides it by the hours it pays for: $4,000 for 160 hours is $25 an hour, so time and a half is $37.50.
overtime.noTaxSummary: From 2025 to 2028 you can deduct the extra half of time and a half for hours over 40 in a week from your federal taxable income, up to $12,500 a year ($25,000 on a joint return). At $20 an hour, 10 overtime hours pay $300, and $100 of it qualifies. The <a:calc>no tax on overtime calculator</a:calc>{note} estimates your deduction and the federal income tax it saves.
overtime.taxTeaser: From 2025 to 2028, the extra half of your overtime pay can be deducted from your federal taxable income.
overtime.taxQualified: {qualified} of this week's overtime counts toward the no tax on overtime deduction.

noTax.aboutTitle: No tax on overtime: how the deduction works
noTax.aboutP1: The <a:irs>deduction for qualified overtime compensation</a:irs> lets you subtract overtime pay from your federal taxable income for 2025 through 2028, whether or not you itemize. It's a deduction, not tax-free pay: your employer still withholds as usual, and Social Security, Medicare and most state taxes still apply.
noTax.aboutP2: Only the premium the Fair Labor Standards Act requires counts: the extra half of time and a half. At $20 an hour, 10 overtime hours pay $300, and $100 of it qualifies. Double time doesn't count double: for the same hours paid at $400, still only $100 qualifies (<a:faq>IRS questions and answers</a:faq>). Overtime that only a state law or a union contract requires, such as daily overtime, doesn't count.
noTax.aboutP3: You can deduct up to $12,500 a year, or $25,000 on a joint return. Over $150,000 of modified adjusted gross income ($300,000 jointly), that limit falls by $100 for each full $1,000, so it's gone at $275,000 ($550,000 jointly). You need a Social Security number valid for work, and married couples must file jointly.
noTax.aboutP4: From 2026, your employer reports qualified overtime in box 12 of your W-2 with code TT, and you claim the deduction on <a:s1a>Schedule 1-A</a:s1a>. You can deduct only what's reported there, so if it's wrong, ask your employer for a corrected W-2c. For 2025, W-2s didn't have to show it, and you could work it out from your pay stubs.
noTax.example: For example, you earn $25 an hour and work 50-hour weeks for 26 weeks of the year. Each of those weeks pays $375 of overtime, and $125 of it qualifies. Over the year that's $3,250, so in the 22% bracket you save about $715 in federal income tax.
noTax.aboutP5: To work out the overtime pay itself, with salaries, bonuses and double time, use the <a:ot>overtime calculator</a:ot>.
noTax.faqA1: No. Only the half the federal law requires counts toward the no tax on overtime deduction, even when you're paid double. For 10 hours at $20 an hour paid at double time, you get $400 and $100 qualifies.
noTax.faqQ2: Do salaried employees get no tax on overtime?
noTax.faqA2: Only if the Fair Labor Standards Act requires their overtime. Non-exempt salaried workers who are paid overtime can deduct the extra half. Exempt employees aren't owed overtime by law, so extra pay for long weeks doesn't qualify.
noTax.faqQ3: Do I still pay Social Security and Medicare on overtime?
noTax.faqA3: Yes. The deduction lowers only federal income tax. Social Security and Medicare (7.65%) and most state income taxes still apply to all your overtime pay.
noTax.faqQ4: When does no tax on overtime end?
noTax.faqA4: It covers tax years 2025 through 2028. Overtime paid in 2029 or later doesn't qualify unless Congress extends it.
age.title: Age calculator: calculate age by date of birth | thetoolproject
age.description: Calculate an exact age from a date of birth in years, months and days, on today or any date, with the weekday of birth and the next birthday.
age.leadStrong: Enter a date of birth to see the exact age.
age.lead: You get years, months and days on today’s date or any other, the age in months, weeks, days and hours, the weekday of the birth and a countdown to the next birthday. It works for babies, children and adults.
age.caption: Counts calendar dates only, so time zones can’t change the answer
home.card.age: Find an exact age in years, months and days from a date of birth.
age.onHint: Today’s date, or pick another, such as a school or visa cutoff date.
age.breakdownEmpty: Enter a date of birth to see the age.
age.errBirthAfter: The date of birth is after the “age on” date. Check the year.
age.errOnInvalid: Enter a full “age on” date, or use today.
age.howStep1: The calculator counts the whole years since the date of birth, then the whole months since the last birthday, then the days left over. Someone born on March 15, 1990 is 36 years, 6 months and 16 days old on October 1, 2026.
age.howStep2: Months are counted from the birth date each time. When a month doesn’t have that day, its last day is used: one month after January 31 is February 28, or February 29 in a leap year.
age.howStep3: The totals count every day between the two dates. Weeks are the days divided by 7, and hours and minutes treat each day as 24 hours, as if the birth were at midnight.
age.howDatesP: Only the calendar dates are used, never the time of day, so the same two dates give the same answer in every time zone and daylight saving time can’t move it. “Today” is today’s date on your device. Everything is worked out in your browser, and the dates you enter aren’t sent anywhere.
age.howChronoTitle: Chronological age for tests and school
age.howChronoP: Chronological age is the exact time since birth, as opposed to a developmental or mental age. Psychologists, speech therapists and teachers use it to score standardized tests, often written as years and months, such as 7;4 for 7 years and 4 months. Some test manuals ask you to count every month as 30 days when you subtract by hand, so their answer can differ from this one by a day or two. If the manual gives a rule, follow it.
age.howBabyTitle: Age calculator for babies and children
age.howBabyP: Babies are usually described in weeks for the first few months, then in months until about age 2. The totals show both: a baby born on June 20, 2026 is 3 months and 11 days, or 14 weeks and 5 days, old on October 1, 2026.
age.faqQ1: How do I calculate age from a date of birth?
age.faqA1: Subtract the birth year from the current year, and if the birthday hasn’t come yet this year, subtract 1 more. For the months, count the whole months since the last birthday, then the days since that date in the latest month. The calculator above does this for any two dates.
age.faqQ2: How do I calculate age from the birth year only?
age.faqA2: Subtract the birth year from this year. That’s the age after this year’s birthday; before it, the age is 1 less. Someone born in 1990 is 36 in 2026 once the birthday has passed, and 35 before that.
age.faqQ3: How old is someone born on February 29?
age.faqA3: In years without a February 29, this calculator counts the birthday on February 28. Laws differ, and some places treat March 1 as the birthday in those years. If it matters for a document or a deadline, check the rule that applies.
age.faqQ4: What is corrected age for a premature baby?
age.faqA4: Corrected age, or adjusted age, is a premature baby’s age minus the number of weeks the baby was born early. A baby born 8 weeks early who is 6 months old has a corrected age of about 4 months. Doctors use it to check growth and development until about age 2 or 3. To see it here, enter the due date as the date of birth: the years, months and days are then the corrected age, but the weekday and next birthday shown are for the due date, not the real birthday.
age.faqQ5: Why do age calculators sometimes disagree by a day?
age.faqA5: Months have different lengths, so the days left over depend on how a calculator counts a month from a date like January 31. This one counts whole months from the birth date and uses the last day of a shorter month. Totals in days and weeks don’t depend on that, so they match in every correct calculator.
