dice.description: Roll dice online: one die or up to 50, d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20, d100 or any number of sides, with a modifier, advantage and disadvantage, 4d6 drop lowest and your last 10 rolls.
dice.lead: Roll one die from 1 to 6, or up to 50 dice at once: d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20, d100 or any number of sides. Add a modifier, roll with advantage or disadvantage for D&D 5e, drop the lowest die for ability scores and see your last 10 rolls.
dice.caption: Every face is equally likely. Rolls use your browser’s secure random numbers
home.card.dice: Roll a d6, a d20 or up to 50 dice, with a modifier and advantage.
dice.empty: Press Roll to see the dice.
dice.modifierHint: Added to the total, such as +5 for an attack bonus or −1.
dice.errCount: Enter a number of dice from {min} to {max}.
dice.errSides: Enter a number of sides from {min} to {max}.
dice.errModifier: Enter a whole number from {min} to {max}, such as +5 or −1.
dice.presetsHint: Advantage rolls two d20 and keeps the higher one, disadvantage keeps the lower one, and an ability score drops the lowest of four d6.
dice.historyEmpty: Your last 10 rolls show up here.
dice.howP1: Choose a die, how many to roll and an optional modifier, then press Roll. Each die is rolled on its own, so two dice can land on the same number. The total adds up the dice that count plus the modifier, and the line under the dice shows the sum.
dice.howP2: The rolls come from your browser’s cryptographically secure random number generator (crypto.getRandomValues), the same source used to make encryption keys. Numbers that would make some faces slightly more likely are thrown away and drawn again, so each face of a d6 comes up 1 time in 6 over the long run. Dice values and totals are never sent to a server, and the dice can’t be set to favor a number.
dice.howNotationP: Games write rolls as XdY+Z: X is the number of dice, Y the number of sides and Z a modifier added to the total. 2d6+3 means rolling two six-sided dice and adding 3, for a total from 5 to 15. A d6 on its own is one six-sided die, and d% or d100 is a number from 1 to 100.
dice.howDndP: Dungeons & Dragons uses the d4, d6, d8, d10, d12 and d20, plus the d100 for percentile tables. These are the rolls you make most often and how to set them up here.
dice.dnd.check.roll: Ability check, attack roll or saving throw
dice.dnd.check.note: Meet or beat the target number, such as the Armor Class or the Difficulty Class (DC).
dice.dnd.advantage.note: Press Advantage under Common rolls and type your bonus in Modifier.
dice.dnd.ability.note: Roll six times and assign the totals to your six abilities. Each total is from 3 to 18.
dice.dnd.damage.note: For example 1d8 for a longsword, 2d6 for a greatsword or 1d12 for a greataxe.
dice.dnd.crit.note: A natural 20 on an attack roll. Roll 2d8 instead of 1d8 for a longsword, then add the modifier once.
dice.dnd.death.note: 10 or higher succeeds. A natural 20 brings you back with 1 hit point, and a natural 1 counts as two failures.
dice.dnd.fireball.note: Fire damage, halved on a successful Dexterity saving throw.
dice.dnd.percentile.note: For random tables. Two d10, one for the tens and one for the ones, give the same 1 to 100.
dice.howDndSource: Rules from the <a:srd>System Reference Document 5.1</a:srd>, published by Wizards of the Coast under a Creative Commons license.
dice.oddsIntro: What each die gives on average, and how likely each total is.
dice.oddsP1: On a fair die every face is equally likely, so the chance of any one number is 1 divided by the number of sides, and the average roll is halfway between 1 and the highest face.
dice.odds2d6Title: Odds of each total with two dice
dice.odds2d6P: Two dice give 36 equally likely results, but the totals aren’t equally likely: there are six ways to roll 7 and only one way each to roll 2 or 12. That’s why 7 is the most common total in board games played with two dice, such as Monopoly and Catan.
dice.oddsAdvantageP: Advantage raises the average d20 roll from 10.5 to about 13.8, and the chance of a natural 20 from 5% to 9.75%. Disadvantage lowers the average to about 7.2. Rolling 4d6 and dropping the lowest gives an average ability score of about 12.2, against 10.5 for a plain 3d6.
dice.faqQ1: Is this dice roller really random?
dice.faqA1: Yes. Each roll uses your browser’s secure random number generator, which can’t be predicted from earlier rolls, and every face is equally likely. Streaks still happen: the same number twice in a row on a d6 comes up 1 time in 6, and over a few dozen rolls some numbers appear more often than others. Dice have no memory, so a number that hasn’t come up for a while isn’t due.
dice.faqQ2: Is it “roll a die” or “roll a dice”?
dice.faqA2: Die is the singular and dice the plural: you roll a die, or you roll two dice. Many people say “a dice” for one, and dictionaries list that as informal. Either way, the roller above rolls one die or up to 50.
dice.faqQ3: How do I roll a random number from 1 to 6?
dice.faqA3: Leave the die on d6 and the number of dice at 1, then press Roll 1d6. You get a whole number from 1 to 6, each with a 1 in 6 chance. For another range that starts at 1, such as 1 to 3 or 1 to 50, choose Custom and enter the highest number as the number of sides.
dice.faqQ4: How do I roll with advantage or disadvantage?
dice.faqA4: Press Advantage under Common rolls. It rolls 2d20 and counts only the higher die; Disadvantage counts only the lower one. Type your bonus in Modifier and it’s added to the die that counts. The faces show both dice, with the one that doesn’t count in gray.
dice.faqQ5: Is this like the Google dice roller?
dice.faqA5: Searching Google for “roll a die” shows a small dice roller in the results. This one rolls the same standard dice and adds the d100, dice with any number of sides from 2 to 1,000, dropping the lowest or highest die, a list of your last 10 rolls and a full screen mode. Bookmark it to roll without searching.
dice.faqQ6: Can I use it in a classroom or for board games?
dice.faqA6: Yes. Press Full screen to show only the dice, the total and the Roll button, in large type for a projector or a tablet on the table. Board games mostly use one or two d6, and the 2d6 button under Common rolls sets that up in one tap. Some phones, including iPhones, don’t let web pages go full screen, so the button doesn’t appear there.

vol.title: Volume calculator: cylinder, cone, tank and pipe volume | thetoolproject
vol.description: Find the volume of a cylinder, rectangular box, cube, cone, sphere, pyramid, prism, pipe or tank, with the formula worked out and the answer in cubic feet, gallons and liters.
vol.leadStrong: Pick a shape and enter its measurements.
vol.lead: Get the volume of a cylinder, rectangular box, cube, cone, sphere, pyramid or prism, how much a pipe holds, or how much liquid is in a vertical, horizontal or rectangular tank. The formula is worked out with your numbers, and the answer is shown in cubic units, liters and gallons.
vol.caption: Answers update as you type. Works in millimeters to yards
vol.tankHint: Use the inside measurements. Cylindrical tanks are taken to have flat ends; rounded ends hold a little more.
vol.formula.tank-horizontal-fill: V = l × (r² × acos((r − f) ÷ r) − (r − f) × √(2 × r × f − f²))
vol.empty: Enter each measurement to see the volume.
vol.errFillTooHigh: The liquid can’t be deeper than the tank is high. For a horizontal tank, that’s its diameter.
vol.errOuterTooSmall: The outside diameter must be larger than the inside diameter.
vol.howP1: Volume is the space a solid takes up, measured in cubic units such as cubic inches (in³) or cubic centimeters (cm³). For a box, multiply length × width × height. For any shape with the same cross-section all the way through, such as a cylinder or a prism, multiply the area of the end by the length. A cone or pyramid holds exactly a third of the cylinder or box it fits in.
vol.howP2: Use one unit for every measurement, and the volume comes out in that unit cubed. The calculator then converts it: 1 cubic foot is 7.48 US gallons, 1 liter is 1,000 cm³, and 1 cubic meter is 1,000 liters.
vol.formulasIntro: The formula for each shape the calculator covers.
vol.note.cylinder: r is the radius (half the diameter) and h the height.
vol.note.box: Length, width and height. A cube is the same with all three equal: V = a³.
vol.note.cone: A third of a cylinder with the same base and height.
vol.note.sphere: r is the radius. A hemisphere is half: V = 2 ÷ 3 × π × r³.
vol.note.pyramid: The base is l by w, and h is the height from the base straight up to the tip.
vol.note.prism: The triangle’s base and height, times the length of the prism.
vol.note.pipe: d is the inside diameter and l the length.
vol.howBoxP: A rectangle is flat, so it has an area but no volume. When people ask for the volume of a rectangle they mean a rectangular box, also called a rectangular prism or cuboid: multiply length × width × height. A room 12 ft long, 10 ft wide and 8 ft high holds 12 × 10 × 8 = 960 cubic feet, or about 35.6 cubic yards.
vol.howCylinderP: Multiply the area of the circular end, π × r², by the height. A can 6 cm across and 10 cm tall has a radius of 3 cm, so its volume is π × 3² × 10 = 282.74 cm³, or about 283 milliliters. If you measured across the circle, choose Diameter and the calculator halves it for you.
vol.howTankTitle: Tank volume and how much is in it
vol.howTankP1: A vertical cylindrical tank holds π × (d ÷ 2)² × h. A tank 4 ft across and 6 ft tall holds 75.4 cubic feet, or about 564 US gallons. Enter the liquid depth to see how much is in it now: in a vertical or rectangular tank, the amount grows evenly with the depth.
vol.howTankP2: A horizontal tank doesn’t fill evenly, because it’s narrow at the bottom and the top and widest in the middle. At a quarter of the depth it’s only 19.6% full, and at half the depth it’s 50% full. The calculator works out the liquid as a <a:segment>circular segment</a:segment> times the length, so the answer is exact for a cylinder with flat ends. Tanks with rounded ends hold a little more.
vol.howPipeP: The water a pipe holds is π × (d ÷ 2)² × l, using the inside diameter. A pipe’s nominal size is a name, not a measurement: a 2-inch Schedule 40 steel pipe is 2.375 in on the outside and 2.067 in on the inside, so 10 ft of it holds about 1.74 US gallons, not the 1.63 a true 2-inch bore would. Check the inside diameter in a <a:pipes>pipe dimension table</a:pipes> or measure it. Add the outside diameter to see the volume of the pipe wall itself.
vol.areaLink: For the area of a flat shape or the surface area of a solid, use the <a:area>area calculator</a:area>.
vol.sources: Conversion factors from <a:nist>NIST’s Guide to the SI, Appendix B</a:nist>: the inch is exactly 2.54 cm and the US gallon 231 cubic inches.
vol.faqQ1: How do you find the volume of a rectangle?
vol.faqA1: Multiply the length, the width and the height: V = l × w × h. A box 4 in long, 3 in wide and 2 in high holds 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 cubic inches. Strictly, that’s a rectangular box (a rectangular prism), because a flat rectangle has no volume.
vol.faqQ2: How many gallons are in a cubic foot?
vol.faqA2: A cubic foot holds 7.48 US gallons, or 28.3 liters. To turn cubic feet into US gallons, multiply by 7.48; to turn cubic inches into gallons, divide by 231. The imperial gallon used in the UK is bigger, so a cubic foot is 6.23 imperial gallons.
vol.faqQ3: How do I work out a cylinder’s volume in gallons?
vol.faqA3: Choose Cylinder and the inch or foot unit, enter the radius or diameter and the height, and read the US gallons under In other units. By hand: work out π × r² × h in cubic inches and divide by 231. A bucket 12 in across and 14 in deep holds π × 6² × 14 = 1,583 cubic inches, about 6.9 gallons.
vol.faqQ4: How do I find how much liquid is in a partly full tank?
vol.faqA4: Choose Tank and its shape, enter its size, then enter how deep the liquid is, measured from the bottom. The readout shows the liquid, and the lines under it show the full tank and how full it is. For a horizontal tank, don’t simply scale by the depth: a quarter of the depth is less than a fifth of the volume.
vol.faqQ5: What’s the difference between volume and capacity?
vol.faqA5: Volume is the space an object takes up, and capacity is how much it can hold. For a thin-walled tank they’re almost the same, but for a thick pipe or a mug the inside is smaller than the outside. Measure on the inside for capacity, which is why the pipe asks for the inside diameter.
vol.faqQ6: What’s the volume of a cone compared with a cylinder?
vol.faqA6: A cone holds exactly a third of a cylinder with the same base and height, so its formula is π × r² × h ÷ 3. A pyramid is a third of the box it fits in in the same way, and a sphere is two thirds of the cylinder it just fits inside.
area.title: Area calculator: circle, triangle, trapezoid and surface area | thetoolproject
area.description: Find the area of a rectangle, square, triangle (including from three sides), circle, trapezoid, parallelogram or ellipse, or the surface area of a cube, box, cylinder, cone, sphere or pyramid, with the formula worked out.
area.leadStrong: Pick a shape and enter its measurements.
area.lead: Get the area of a rectangle, square, triangle, circle, trapezoid, parallelogram or ellipse, or the surface area of a cube, box, cylinder, cone, sphere or pyramid. The formula is worked out with your numbers, and the answer is shown in square units, acres and hectares, with the perimeter where the shape gives one.
area.caption: Answers update as you type. A triangle works from its base and height or its three sides
area.formula.solid-box: A = 2 × (l × w + l × h + w × h)
area.formula.solid-cylinder: A = 2 × π × r² + 2 × π × r × h
area.formula.solid-cone: A = π × r² + π × r × s
area.empty: Enter each measurement to see the area.
area.lateral: Side area without the base or ends: {area}.
area.errNotTriangle: These sides can’t make a triangle: the longest side must be shorter than the other two added together.
area.howP1: Area is the space inside a flat shape, measured in square units such as square feet (ft²) or square meters (m²). For a rectangle, multiply length × width. A triangle is half of a rectangle with the same base and height, and a parallelogram is a rectangle with one end cut off and moved to the other, so it’s base × height too.
area.howP2: Use one unit for every measurement, and the area comes out in that unit squared. Square units grow fast: 1 square foot is 144 square inches, 1 square yard is 9 square feet, and an acre is 43,560 square feet.
area.formulasIntro: The formula for each flat shape the calculator covers.
area.note.rectangle: Length times width. A square is the same with both equal: A = a².
area.note.triangle-base: The height is measured at a right angle to the base, not along a side.
area.note.triangle-sides: Heron’s formula, for when you know the three sides. s is half the perimeter.
area.note.circle: r is the radius, half the diameter.
area.note.trapezoid: a and b are the two parallel sides; h is the distance between them.
area.note.parallelogram: The height is at a right angle to the base, not the slanted side.
area.note.ellipse: a and b are half the longest and shortest widths.
area.surfaceIntro: The total area of every face of a solid, as if you unfolded it flat.
area.note.solid-box: Three pairs of rectangles: top and bottom, front and back, the two ends.
area.note.solid-cylinder: Two circles plus the side, which unrolls into a rectangle 2 × π × r long and h high.
area.note.solid-cone: The base plus the side. s is the slant height, √(r² + h²).
area.note.solid-sphere: Exactly four times the area of a circle with the same radius.
area.note.solid-pyramid: The square base plus four triangles. s is the slant height, √((a ÷ 2)² + h²).
area.howCircleP: Multiply π by the radius squared. A circle 10 in across has a radius of 5 in, so its area is π × 5² = 78.54 square inches, and the distance around it is 31.42 in. If you measured across the circle, choose Diameter: squaring the diameter instead of the radius is the most common mistake, and gives an answer four times too big.
area.howTriangleP: With the base and the height, the area is base × height ÷ 2. When you only know the three sides, choose Three sides and the calculator uses Heron’s formula: a triangle with sides 3, 4 and 5 has s = 6 and an area of √(6 × 3 × 2 × 1) = 6. Three lengths only make a triangle when the longest is shorter than the other two together.
area.howTrapezoidP: Average the two parallel sides, then multiply by the height between them. A trapezoid with parallel sides of 6 and 10 and a height of 4 has an area of (6 + 10) ÷ 2 × 4 = 32. Outside North America the shape is usually called a trapezium.
area.howSurfaceP: Surface area adds up the area of every face, which is what you need for paint, wrapping or sheet material. A cylinder 3 cm in radius and 10 cm high has two circles of π × 3² and a side of 2 × π × 3 × 10, for 245.04 cm² in total. For a cone or pyramid the calculator works out the slant height from the height you enter, so you don’t have to measure along the slope.
area.volumeLink: For the space inside a solid, use the <a:volume>volume calculator</a:volume>.
area.sources: Heron’s formula as given by <a:heron>Wolfram MathWorld</a:heron>. Conversion factors from <a:nist>NIST’s Guide to the SI, Appendix B</a:nist>: an acre is 43,560 square feet and a hectare 10,000 square meters.
area.faqQ1: How do you find the area of a circle from the diameter?
area.faqA1: Halve the diameter to get the radius, then multiply π by the radius squared. A circle 8 ft across has a radius of 4 ft and an area of π × 4² = 50.27 square feet. You can also use π × d² ÷ 4, which gives the same answer.
area.faqQ2: How do I find the area of a triangle without the height?
area.faqA2: If you know all three sides, use Heron’s formula: choose Triangle, then Three sides. If you know two sides and the angle between them, the area is a × b × sin(C) ÷ 2. For a right triangle, the two shorter sides are the base and the height.
area.faqQ3: How do I work out the square feet of a room?
area.faqA3: Measure the length and the width in feet and multiply them: a room 12 ft by 15 ft is 180 square feet. For an L-shaped room, split it into two rectangles, find each area and add them. Buy about 10% more flooring than the area to allow for cuts.
area.faqQ4: How many square feet are in an acre?
area.faqA4: An acre is 43,560 square feet, or about 4,047 square meters. A hectare is 10,000 square meters, about 2.47 acres. Measure a plot in feet or meters and the calculator shows the acres and hectares under In other units.
area.faqQ5: What’s the difference between area and surface area?
area.faqA5: Area measures a flat shape. Surface area is the total area of all the faces of a solid, such as the six faces of a box. Both are in square units. The space inside a solid is its volume, in cubic units.
area.faqQ6: How do I find the area of an irregular shape?
area.faqA6: Split it into shapes the calculator covers, such as rectangles, triangles and half circles, find the area of each and add them. For a shape with a curved edge, many small rectangles or triangles give a close estimate.
harAnalyzer.title: HAR analyzer and HAR file viewer: open .har files online | thetoolproject
harAnalyzer.description: Open and analyze HAR files online, free and with no upload. See every request’s status, size, timing, headers and response, find errors and slow calls, and remove cookies before sharing.
harAnalyzer.leadStrong: Open a HAR file to see what the browser loaded.
harAnalyzer.lead: Every request is listed with its status, size and timing on a waterfall. Filter for errors, read the headers and responses, and download a copy without cookies. The file is read in this browser and never uploaded.
harAnalyzer.caption: .har files from Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, up to 200 MB, no upload
harAnalyzer.howTitle: How to read a HAR file
harAnalyzer.howIntro: Choose or drop a .har file, or try the example. The analyzer lists every request in the order it started, with the number of requests, errors, bytes transferred and the total time at the top. Click a column heading to sort, for example by Time to find the slowest requests or by Size to find the largest.
harAnalyzer.howFindP: Choose {errors} to show only requests that failed or returned a 4xx or 5xx status, or filter by type, such as Fetch/XHR for API calls. Type part of a URL to narrow the list. The waterfall shows when each request started and how long it took, so requests that waited on others stand out.
harAnalyzer.howDetailP: Click a request to open its details: the request and response headers, the query string and request body, the response body (JSON is formatted and images are shown), the cookies, and a timing breakdown from DNS lookup to content download. Responses are shown as text and never run, so a saved page can’t execute scripts here.
harAnalyzer.openTitle: How to open a HAR file
harAnalyzer.openP: A HAR file is plain JSON text, so any text editor can open it, but even a small recording is hard to read that way. To see it as a list of requests, drop it on this page. In Chrome and Edge you can also drag the file onto the Network tab of the developer tools.
harAnalyzer.createTitle: How to create a HAR file
harAnalyzer.createChrome: Chrome and Edge: open the developer tools with F12 (Cmd+Option+I on a Mac), go to the Network tab, tick Preserve log, reload the page and repeat the problem, then click the Export HAR button (the download arrow) and save the file. Recent versions of Chrome leave cookies and sign-in headers out of the export unless you turn that on in the developer tools settings.
harAnalyzer.createFirefox: Firefox: open the Network panel with Ctrl+Shift+E (Cmd+Option+E on a Mac), reload the page and repeat the problem, then right-click any request and choose Save All As HAR.
harAnalyzer.createSafari: Safari: turn on Show features for web developers in Settings, Advanced, open Web Inspector with Cmd+Option+I, go to the Network tab, repeat the problem and click Export.
harAnalyzer.whatP: HAR (HTTP Archive) is a JSON format that records a browser’s network activity: for each request, the URL, method, headers, cookies, status, timing and often the response body. Browsers export it from their developer tools, and support teams ask for one to see what went wrong on a page. The format is described in the <a:spec>HAR 1.2 specification</a:spec>.
harAnalyzer.privacyTitle: Before you share a HAR file
harAnalyzer.privacyP: A HAR file can hold everything sent and received while recording, including cookies, sign-in tokens, form fields and personal data in responses. {sanitize} saves a copy with the cookie lists emptied and the values of the Cookie, Set-Cookie and Authorization headers, and of headers whose names contain token, key, secret, session, CSRF or password, replaced with [removed]. URLs, request bodies and responses are kept as they are, so check them before you share the file.
harAnalyzer.limitsP: This tool opens .har files, and HAR data saved as .json, up to 200 MB, from Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari, Charles, Fiddler and other tools that write HAR 1.2. Large files need a lot of memory, so a phone may not open the largest ones. Response bodies longer than 500,000 characters are shown in part and can be downloaded in full.
harAnalyzer.faqA1: No. The file is read and analyzed on your device, and nothing in it is sent anywhere. That matters, because HAR files often contain cookies and sign-in tokens.
harAnalyzer.faqQ2: Why are some response bodies missing?
harAnalyzer.faqA2: A response body is only in the file if the browser saved it when exporting. Requests that failed, were redirected or were cancelled have no body, and some browsers leave out large or binary responses. The analyzer says when a body wasn’t saved.
harAnalyzer.faqQ3: What do the timing phases mean?
harAnalyzer.faqA3: Queued and stalled is time spent waiting to start, DNS lookup finds the server’s address, the initial connection opens it (including the TLS handshake for HTTPS), request sent is the upload, waiting for server response is the time to the first byte, and content download is the time to receive the rest.
harAnalyzer.faqQ4: What does a Failed status mean?
harAnalyzer.faqA4: The request got no HTTP response: it was blocked, for example by an ad blocker, cancelled, or failed on the network. Open the request to see the error the browser recorded, such as net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT.
